title: Yehudah ben Tamuza
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In Jerusalem Talmud Megillah 4:5, Rabbi Yonah and Rabbi Yose went up to visit the brother of Yehudah ben Tamuza, a relative of Rabbi Yose, son of R' Chanina.

notes.text: למיחמיה is an ordinary Aramaic form of “to see”; it need not be emended to למיחזיה. The final “relative of Rabbi Yose son of Rabbi Chanina” may attach to the brother or to Yehudah; the source position is retained. No condolence visit is added.

The saved whole Guggenheimer JerusalemTalmudMegillah4:5 scalar has full Rabbi Yonah and Rabbi Yose going to visit the brother of Yehudah bar Tamuza. The seeing/visiting form is legitimate Aramaic, not a proved corruption; condolence is not imported. Source ben Tamuza and named bar Tamuza remain distinct. The named kinship phrase has Yose ben Chanina without a full paternal Rabbi title, whereas Hyman abbreviates that title; R' Chanina is retained. The relative’s attachment remains open rather than an admitted family identity.

In Guggenheimer’s Jerusalem Talmud Megillah 4:5:3 the visit takes place at a synagogue, and “relative of Rabbi Yose ben Chanina” follows Yehudah bar Tamuza. The phrase can describe either Yehudah or his brother. The photographed Hyman notice has ben Tamuza and appears to read למיחזיה, alongside למיחמיה in the supplied text. Both convey seeing or visiting here.
